findings.title: Client mutation uses raw fetch without error handling and calls res.json() on a 204 response
findings.rationale: The `useDismissAllSuggestions` mutation calls `fetch` directly and unconditionally calls `res.json()` on the response. The server returns a 204 No Content with no body, so `res.json()` will throw a `SyntaxError` (or return `undefined` depending on the runtime). Additionally, the code does not check `res.ok` before parsing, so any non-2xx response (e.g., 404, 500) will also be parsed as JSON and returned as data rather than thrown as an `ApiError`. This violates rule 3: client code must throw `ApiError` on non-2xx responses to preserve the error code, message, and status for the UI. The fix is to use `apiFetch` (which handles errors and 204 correctly) or to check `res.ok` and throw `ApiError` with the error body, and handle the 204 case by returning `null` instead of calling `res.json()`.

findings.title: Client mutation calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response
findings.rationale: The server returns HTTP 204 with no body, but the client calls `res.json()` which will reject because the response body is empty. This causes the mutation to fail on every successful call, breaking the 'Dismiss all suggestions' feature for all users. The caller is the web client (FindingsPanel).

findings.title: Client mutation does not throw ApiError on non-2xx responses
findings.rationale: The mutation uses raw `fetch` and, on a non-2xx response, calls `res.json()` and returns the error body as data. This means error responses are treated as success data, and the UI will not show the server's error message, status, or code. The project convention (rule 3) requires throwing `ApiError` for all non-2xx responses.

findings.title: Client does not surface errors as `ApiError` when using raw `fetch`
findings.rationale: The mutation uses `fetch` directly and does not check `res.ok`. On a non-2xx response, `res.json()` will parse the error body but the mutation will succeed with the error data, and `onSuccess` will invalidate queries. The codebase convention (rule 3) requires throwing `ApiError` so that callers can handle errors consistently. This also means the button will not show error feedback.

findings.title: Client mutation calls `res.json()` on a 204 No Content response, breaking the feature
findings.rationale:
The server returns 204 with no body. `res.json()` on an empty body throws a `SyntaxError`. The mutation throws, so `onSuccess` never fires and the query invalidation (`qc.invalidateQueries`) never runs. The user clicks the button, the request succeeds, but the UI does not refresh — the feature is invisible to the caller.

**Caller that breaks:** Web client (the `FindingsPanel` component).

**Compatible alternative:** Either (a) change the server to return a JSON body (e.g., 200 with `{ success: true }`) and keep `res.json()`, or (b) change the client to not parse JSON on a 204 — e.g., `return res;` and adjust the mutation to not expect data. Since the PR description explicitly says 204, option (b) is the minimal fix.

findings.title: Client mutation does not check `res.ok` before parsing JSON, swallowing server errors
findings.rationale:
The mutation calls `fetch` directly and, on a non-2xx response, returns the error body as data instead of throwing an `ApiError`. This violates the project's error-handling pattern (rule 3). The caller (`FindingsPanel`) will not see the server's error code or message, and the mutation will resolve successfully with the error payload, so `onError` never fires. The user sees no feedback when the request fails.

**Caller that breaks:** Web client (any component using `useDismissAllSuggestions`).

**Compatible alternative:** Check `res.ok` and, if false, read the error body and throw an `ApiError` (as done in `client/src/lib/api.ts:44-58`).

findings.title: Client does not throw ApiError on non-2xx responses
findings.rationale: The mutation uses `fetch` directly and does not check `res.ok`. On a server error (e.g., 404, 500), it will attempt `res.json()` and either throw a generic Error or return the error body as data. The project convention (rule 3) requires throwing `ApiError` so that pages can display the server's error code and message. This loses error information for the user.

findings.rationale: The mutation function calls `fetch` directly and unconditionally returns `res.json()` without checking `res.ok`. findings.title: Client mutation omits credentials, causing unauthenticated requests
findings.rationale: The `fetch` call does not include `credentials: 'include'`. The server route uses `getContext` which requires authentication via cookies. Without credentials, the request will be rejected (401/403) and the feature will silently fail. All other client API calls in the codebase use `apiFetch` which includes credentials.
